en: Preface to the Great Affairs of the Forest Monasteries:
I have occupied a position within the forest monasteries for barely thirty years. I have seen many of the great elders of the present age.

Yet, though I have grown weary of the world and closed my door beneath Mount Danqiu and Zhongfeng, living daily alongside the grasses and trees as if liberated from them, old habits remain unextinguished; I am prone to dozing.
After my sleep, I reached for a box of antiques at random and found a volume titled *Luohu Yalu* (The Wild Record of Luohu) composed by Master Ying of Jiangxi.
Upon opening the scroll, the first thing I encountered was a preface and introduction written by Master Wuzhuo, which stated:

"Regarding the机缘 (karmic conditions) through which former sages entered the Way, most Chan records do not fully record them. This oversight lies with the fact that the eminent talents of that time failed to compile and arrange them."

It was not out of a desire to protect my own lineage or propagate the Dharma that I did so; consequently, those who would look upon the worthy and seek to emulate them can do nothing but sigh in lamentation.
Upon carefully savoring these words, they truly serve as a corrective for the malady of indolence within our own ranks.

Therefore, I have recalled the various sayings of my predecessors—words that were witnessed and heard by the public and which remain applicable and worth recording in recent times—and have compiled them into this single volume. Written here.
It was completed and presented to the elder Fo-zhao of Mount Mao. Upon seeing it, he was delighted and said to his attendant Daoquan, "This is truly a great event for our school.
Why not carve it into woodblocks to transmit it to future generations? He thus titled it *Conglin Shengshi* (Great Events of the Monastic Community).
Whether this work brings me praise or reproach, let there be no cause for derision.
Preface by Daorong on the first fascicle of the *Chronicles of the Great Events of the Forests*, written on a mid-autumn day in the third year of the Qingyuan era,

Grand Councilor Cheng visited National Teacher Nanchan. Nanchan instructed him to contemplate the "karmic affinity" (shengyuan) koan.
One day, Fachang asked, "Why do you not simply cut it off for him right now? Nanchan replied, "I have already been drawing feet on a snake for him;
it is he himself who has failed to see through it. Fachang asked, "How would you act for him, Master? Nanchan said, "I would chew up all the ginger and drink it all down."
"Vinegar. Fachuang said, "The worldly masters go about in this manner again. Nanquan asked, "What would Fachang do?
Fachang took up his whisk and struck him. Nanquan said, "This old fellow is so heartless! Fachang then desisted.
One day, while Fo-yin was entering his room for seated meditation, Dongpo suddenly arrived. Fo-yin said, "There are no mats or seats here;
I am unable to attend to you, Layman. Dongpo replied, "I shall temporarily borrow the four elements of the Master’s body as my seat.
Fo-yin said, "I have a question for you, Layman. If you can answer it, you may sit; if you cannot, you must forfeit your jade belt."
Sūshan replied with delight, "I accept your invitation. Yìn said, "Just now, Layman, you said you would borrow this mountain monk’s four great elements as a bed and seat.
But since the mountain monk’s four great elements are fundamentally empty and the five aggregates do not exist, where will you sit?"
Sūshun hesitated and was unable to offer a further reply. He then untied his jade belt, laughed heartily, and departed.
Zhiyuan, however, presented him with a *yunshan* (cloud-mountain) patched robe. Sūshun composed a verse which says: "A hundred thousand lamps form a single lamp-light;

All are the wondrous Dharma Kings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Therefore, East Slope dares not begrudge it; I lend you my four elements to serve as a meditation couch. He also spoke of his "sickly bones."
How difficult it is to bear this jade belt encircling the waist; those of dull faculties still fall under the mechanism of the arrow’s point.
One day, I shall beg for food in the courtesans’ quarters, to trade for my old monastic robe from the clouds and mountains. It is further said: This belt has seen men as numerous as way-stations;

its transmission reaching this point is truly leisurely. Its brocade patterns are scattered yet perfectly harmonious; I shall give it to the old man Wan-hui, who feigns madness. He sealed this with two verses.
Xie said: "Shishuang seized Pei Xiu’s ceremonial tablet; for three hundred years, the multitude has praised it with one voice.

How can this compare to Su Dongpo leaving behind his jade belt? It shall forever harmonize with the bright moon, both flawless. He also said: "Bian He of Jing Mountain presented [the jade] to three reigns;
Zhao Gao of the State of Zhao returned from ten thousand deaths. A supreme treasure should only be used by the Son of Heaven; why was it left behind on this small Penglai?"
One day, Provincial Inspector Yang Cigong asked Zen Master Fu Rong Kai, "How many years has it been since we last met?
Kai replied, "Seven years. Yang said, "During these seven years, have you been practicing Chan or studying the Way? Kai replied, "I have not been beating that drum or playing those pipes.
Yang said, "If that is so, then you have merely traveled through mountains and waters, accomplishing nothing at all. Kai replied, "It is as you say."

Not long after they had parted, Yang Hehe laughed heartily, remarking, "You have truly discerned this with great clarity. Later, when Han Wei Gong came to visit during the summer, Foyan Kai went out to receive him.
Han said, "The imperial palace gates are closed and no one may go out; why have you broken the precepts by coming here? Kai replied, "In official matters, not even a needle is permitted;
in private matters, carriages and horses pass through freely. Han was greatly pleased.
Chan Master Zhenjing resided at Dayu in Jiyin. When Governor Qian Gongyi came to visit, he marveled that the number of practitioners had suddenly increased;
they had all flocked there because the Master possessed virtue and wisdom. Governor Qian entered the Master’s quarters, yet he found nothing extraordinary about him.
The following day, he ordered a vegetarian feast. As the Master took his seat, a dog suddenly escaped from behind the screen curtains. The Master—
He moved away from him a short distance. Qian mocked him, saying, "A great *kalyāṇamitra* is surely able to subdue dragons and tame tigers; how could he fear a dog?

The Master replied instantly, "It is easy to subdue a tiger that crouches on a crag, but difficult to bring down a dragon that guards its dwelling. Qian was greatly pleased and subsequently moved his residence to Shengshou Monastery to seek the Way from him.
When Chengtian Zong was traveling on pilgrimage, he sent a letter to the Venerable Xiyin of Quanzhou, which arrived at the residence of Li, the Imperial Prince.
Upon meeting, the Commandery Marshal asked, "For what reason have you come to the capital? Zong replied, "I have come specifically to deliver a letter for the monastery.
The Marshal said, "Just now, I regret that I did not pose a question. Zong said, "The Commandery Marshal is accustomed to seizing such opportunities. The Marshal then—
"Hai! Zong said. "I have let you off with one stroke. Wei said, "A second offense will not be tolerated.
Zong said, "Thirty years from now, there will be many who cite this. Wei laughed heartily.
When Chan Master Xingyang Pou was first serving as the head gardener at Dayang, he was planting melons. As he was working, Dayang asked, "When will the sweet melons ripen?
Pou replied, "They have already ripened right now. Dayang said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here. Pou asked, "To whom would you give them so they could eat them?
Dayang said, "Give them to those who do not enter the garden. Pou asked, "I do not know for certain who it is that does not enter..."
Yangshan asked, "Guanzi, have you eaten yet? Guanzi replied, "I have not. Yangshan said, "Do you recognize him? Guanzi said, "Even though I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him.
Yangshan smiled and departed. Later, Guanzi fell ill. Yangshan came to visit him and asked, "This body is like an illusionary bubble;

it is within this illusionary bubble that one accomplishes the Great Matter. If there were no such illusionary bubble, there would be no way to accomplish the Great Matter. If you wish to accomplish the Great Matter, you must recognize [it]."
Yangshan asked, "What is it to grasp a bubble-like illusion? Xuanjue said, "That is still a matter of this side. Yangshan asked, "What is a matter of that side?
Xuanjue said, "The crimson sun shines across the earth; no flowers bloom at the bottom of the sea. Yangshan laughed and said, "Is that how you remain so alert?
Xuanjue gave a shout and said, "I thought you had forgotten! Thereafter, Xuanjue never rose again from his seat. Yangshan then presented him with a monastic robe (*zhiduo*) and—
The verse was entrusted to Fushan Yuan. Later, Yuan received Touzi Qing, thereby founding the Dongshan school.
○ Chan Master Fayun Yuan-tong Xiu initially studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. One day, he sighed and said:

"I observe that when Sudhana first saw Mañjuśrī, he subsequently traveled through over a hundred cities to serve fifty-three spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Furthermore, I have heard of Bodhidharma..."
"The Old Lu came from the West; he went southward, transmitting the Unsurpassed Mind-Seal outside the teachings.

How could I merely remain within one region, stagnating in the schools of Nature (xìng) and Characteristics (xiàng)? Therefore, I abandoned my studies, packed my bags, and traveled south to visit Master Huai at Wúwéi."
Huai asked, "What sutra does the Master lecture upon? Xiu replied, "I have studied the *Avataṃsaka* roughly. Huai asked, "What is the central tenet of the *Avataṃsaka*?
Xiu replied, "It takes the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) as its tenet. Huai asked, "What is the central tenet of the Dharma-realm? Xiu replied:

Huai said, "I take the mind as the fundamental principle. Daohui asked, "What do you take the mind to be the fundamental principle of? Xiu was unable to answer. Huai said, "A difference of a hair's breadth results in worlds apart.
You must accept it yourself; then there will be an awakening. Seventeen days later, he heard a monk cite [the teaching]. At that moment, he attained realization.
Bai Zhao asked Baoci, "It is said that 'sentiment arises and wisdom is obstructed; conceptualization changes and the essence becomes distinct.
Before sentiment has arisen, what is it like? Baoci replied, "Obstructed. At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He went straight to the abbot’s quarters to present his realization.
Baoci said with joy, "Many masters have come to see me before and after, but you alone are worthy to inherit the Great Dharma. My school shall, in days to come, rest upon you."
One day, [Yunmen] said, "I am going alone. The Master (Dongshan) then served him diligently for eight years. Huai-tui was regarded as his foremost disciple.
He emerged into the world at Shu’s Sideshansi and later resided at Fayun Monastery in Dongjing. From this point on, the orthodox lineage of Yunmen was extensively propagated.
Furong Kai was serving as the kitchen steward at Touzi. One day, Touzi asked him, "The duties of the kitchen office are no easy matter.
Kai replied, "I do not dare to say they are. Touzi asked, "Are you cooking porridge? Or steaming rice? Kai said, "The laborers wash the rice and light the fires."
A practitioner was boiling congee and steaming rice. The Master’s son asked, "What are you doing? Kai replied, "Out of compassion, the Master has let me go idle.
Touzi was startled by this.
Chengyin asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk said, "Xichuan. Chengyin asked, "When did you leave your hometown?
The monk said, "The second month of last year. Chengyin asked, "How do you express the phrase 'not yet having left one's native land'?"
The monk said, "Your whole body is a mouth; it is difficult to provide an answer. Cheng said, "That is still a phrase about leaving home and losing one's occupation.
The monk was speechless. Cheng struck once with his whisk and said, "In vain you have worn through so many straw sandals."
Master Fuxin Cai of Gushan was a native of Min. Initially, he went to study under Sishin. Sishin asked, "Where is your home district? Cai replied, "Fuzhou.
Sishin said, "Xiansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river. Why have you come here?
Cai replied, "While walking, it does not hinder one from swinging one's arms. Sishin said, "Swing them with the left hand? Swing them with the right hand? Cai then let go.

He threw both hands out and felt great joy in his heart. Once he had been granted permission to stay, he was crowded out by an attendant monk who said, "You have been causing a disturbance in monasteries everywhere you go;
the Master must not allow you to remain here. Thereupon, the Master refused him entry, saying, "I have heard that you cause disturbances in monasteries wherever you go;
go elsewhere for now. Cai then asked, "Where is the eye of a Great Good Knowledge (Mahāvidvān)?"
He took his place, then brushed out his sleeves and departed. He went to see Zhao Mo, who received him. Before long, he attained realization of the Way of Huanglong.
Zhao Mo then entrusted him with the responsibility of the Great Dharma.
Master Yuequan Zhang An Dao, while serving as the Prefect of Chuzhou during the Qingli era, visited a monastery.

Seeing that the Buddhist scriptures were neatly arranged, he took one out of curiosity and read it; it was the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*. He was struck with a sense of wonder, as if he had recovered a long-lost possession.
Upon closely examining the calligraphy and the handwriting, they appeared exactly like his own. Overcome with grief and joy, he sighed deeply. Following this...
This was his realization. He once used the four opening verses of a sutra to elucidate the essential point of the mind.

When Dongpo visited Nandu, he personally witnessed the Master speak thus and entrusted him with three hundred thousand coins, saying, "Use these to print and distribute [the text] throughout the Jianghuai region. Dongpo then wrote it out with his own hand.
He commissioned the Buddha to be engraved upon Mount Jinshan. Thus, the poem he presented to Yuequan contains the lines:
"The Layman Yuequan delights in Heaven; the chamber of Vimalakīrti is empty and serene."
Xuetang Xing was a native of Kuocang. Having entered the provincial academy in his youth, he was moved to deep compassion upon witnessing the slaughter of living beings.
He subsequently abandoned his home and traveled directly to Puzhao Wangsi Temple in Sizhou to take ordination, making the sweeping of the pagoda his primary duty.
Once his hair had been shorn, he went to Longmen in Shu to serve as an attendant to Chan Master Foyan, wearing a single robe through both winter and summer.
Furthermore, he raised lice, for which his neighbors and those on his shoulders all felt weary of him. He would sit in meditation daily in secluded places within the hall.
One day, while contemplating the story of Xuansha striking his own toe, he made a great breakthrough in realization. Foyan was a native of Sichuan; once, during his ascent to the hall, he said:
While attending him as he stood by, [Zhaozhou] said jokingly, "The monks of Sichuan are coarse; the monks of Zhejiang are elegant. If you all do not believe me, look at my attendant.
The entire assembly burst into loud laughter. Later, when his father was leaving his post as Grand Music Master to take up the governorship of Sanqu, his mother came to see him off.
Because her son was dressed in such tattered rags, the gatekeeper refused to let him enter more than twice.

Xing then took off her clothes and gave them to her. As soon as they had barely covered her, her mother heard the news and, unable to contain herself, collapsed to the ground, crying out, "Is my child still alive?
She then brought her into the main hall of the residence and compelled her to change her clothes and bathe.
During the bath, all her old clothes were stripped away, leaving her with nothing but the new ones she was made to wear. Xing wept and said, "For how many years have I been his consort; how could..."
"How can you suddenly abandon me? he cried. He then went to Jixiang Temple to stay for the night.
The next day, his parents, brothers, and others all came to pay their respects, but he departed at dawn; they did not even manage to see him. They only saw a verse left upon the wall which said:
"Do not disdain a heart like iron; Even one's own self is a source of resentment. Only when the snow before the gate has been swept away Will the fire within be opened."
Lian: "Do not ask anything further; all things are equally the forgetting of conditions. When this matter corresponds, the Vajra-seed manifests before you.
His mother lost her sight due to grief for her teacher, so he traveled back to Kuāngcāng. His father pressured him to enter the monastic life at Nánmíng, and he later moved to Wūjù in Qú.
His Way flourished greatly, and he passed away at Jiànfú in Ráo. Miàoxī personally [performed his funeral rites].
The preface to his *Collected Records* was circulated throughout the world.
○ Master Dianniu was a native of Chengdu; his surname was Zheng and his given name was Tianyou. He was originally from an official family.

Having first taken the examination at the local prefectural school and subsequently at Zizhou, he passed both. However, Tianyou did not dare to accept these honors; he changed his name and fled through the mountain passes, eventually arriving at a mountain monastery.
When the Daoist Tu returned to the west, [Zhaozhou] saw that his bearing was extraordinary and his discourse was transcendent; he therefore traveled down the river with him on the same boat.

They eventually went to Mount Lu to shave their heads, whereupon [Tu] did not change his original name. He first visited Sishi, but there was no spiritual resonance; he then relied upon Zantang at Letan.
At that time, Miaoxi was serving as the attendant, and Tu resided in the library office, following him morning and night. Later, [Miaoxi] went to...
The ancient Yaoshan clarified the Great Matter. He appeared in the world at Xiaobaofeng on Mount Lu and later resided at Yunyan.
He once composed a verse in response to Zhong Daozhe’s “Verses on Herding an Ox,” which says: "Two horns point to heaven; four hooves tread the earth.

Having snapped the nose-rope, he herds nothing but dung and gas. Initially, Zhang Wujin saw that he was straightforward and unconcerned with worldly affairs, and he often looked down upon him, calling him a madman.
Later, Miaoxi presented this verse to Wujin. As Wujin struck the desk in appreciation, Miaoxi asked, "Governor, tell me, who composed this verse?
Wujin replied, "Were it not for the Great Being Maitreya, who else could have uttered such words?
Miaoxi said, "This was actually composed by Dianyou the day before yesterday. Wujin exclaimed, "How marvelous! How marvelous!"
"How extraordinary! Does the Zantang Monastery have such a son? The single lineage of Linji rests upon this man.
However, I had merely pawned him away in the pawnshop for one hundred strings of cash. With my own physical eyes, I failed to recognize him; I nearly let such a person slip through my fingers.
Consequently, I burned incense, gazed toward Yunyan, and repented my error. Later, after leaving Yunyan, You traveled to Qixian on Mount Lu. Long...
When the Old Man saw that Jianlao was also emitting a "river-like" air, he refused to let him stay and said, "Old man, you are truly like a cow being pledged at a pawnshop.
Upon hearing this, You composed a verse and departed, saying: "When has a pawnshop ever been able to pledge a cow?
It is only because the price is so high it is difficult to repay. I suspect your capital is not very great; How could you possibly [afford such a pledge]?"
Yong was a man from Wuning; for forty years he remained there until the end of his life, never venturing outside.
When Tudu saw him, he was already ninety-three years old.
Fodeng Xun, whose style name was Tianmo, was a native of Anji in Huzhou. He succeeded Fojian and resided at Heshan.
Once, while presiding over the assembly, a monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? He replied, "The traveler’s road is as vast as heaven;
the lord’s gate is as deep as the sea. "What is the host within the guest? He said, "Often, because of seeing off guests far away, one remembers the time of leaving home. It was like this.
"What is 'the guest within the host'? He replied: "When meeting, one does not dismount; each has their own path ahead. "How is 'the host within the host'? He replied:
"Once the ancestral decree is issued, who is the one who dares to step forward? "Is there still a matter beyond [the distinction of] guest and host?
He replied: "Bring forth the question regarding that which is beyond. "What is the matter beyond? He replied: "If the great ocean were to know contentment..."
"The hundred rivers should flow backward. When the monks prostrated, Xun said, "This is what I have learned as an elder monk over thirty years.
○ The practitioner Kefu Ning was a native of Hexi. He visited Wuzu Yan; Yan observed that he stood with an air of lofty superiority.
Yanshou’s discernment was preeminent; whenever the assembly praised him, they would further appoint him as an attendant in the Hall.

His fellow students grew envious of him and, at night, lured him to the Ning Mountain to engage in ritual circumambulation and discourse. They then assaulted him, wounding his face and eyes so severely that he could no longer attend the assembly.

When Yuancheng heard of this, he went in person to visit him and asked, "I hear you have been treated with such discourtesy by a certain group. Why do you not go to the Abbot’s quarters to clear your grievance? Yanshou replied, "I am listening."
The old monk pursued you; how could I ever bear not to reveal this? He simply said, "I injured myself while falling; it was no one else's fault.
Yan shed tears and said, "My power of endurance is not equal to yours. What will you do to me in the days to come?

Later, he appeared in the world at Kaifu Temple and accommodated a congregation of five hundred. When he was about to pass away, he fixed the date and time for his parinirvāṇa, sitting upright to depart while entrusting the Great Dharma.
He conferred the fruit [of realization] upon Yue’an. Guo sank like a stone to the bottom of the crowd; no one could recognize him, except for Yuanwu, who later enabled him to emerge into the world.
He sent him off with this verse: "The final word of the Old Man of Mount Xi, Truly transmitted to the Hall of Four Excellences.
The true command has been issued, its wind chilling and fierce; The sword-spirit between the stars illuminates the light of heaven."
When Ying’an first relied upon Yuanwu at Mount Jiangshan, he and Ciyun Yuan were companions. When Yuan resided at Lianyun, Hu arrived from the assembly of Foyan Liao of Mount Huqiu.
Upon his initial arrival, [Yuan] immediately appointed him as the Head Seat (shouzuo). Not long after, he was ordered to conduct the formal ceremony for the ordination of monks (lisheng).
Yuan ascended the hall and said: "The Lion roams the West River; Lianyun brings forth the tiger and rhinoceros. [Hu] personally...
Coming from within the den of a fierce tiger, his patterns, claws, and fangs are all fully present. Though he has not yet startled the herds, he already possesses the ambition to devour an ox.
Alas, how I grieve that the lineage of Yangqi is being treated like a broom sweeping the floor! Raising up an iron backbone to avenge my late master—do you all recognize him?
His two eyes are as large as rings; it is he who stands directly before you. Later, he appeared in the world.
Miaoyan served as the incense-bearer at Tiger Hill. Thereafter, he resided there for ten years; his Way rivaled that of Miaoxi.
Minister Li Hao had been a close associate of the Master for a long time and once praised the Master’s portrait, saying: "Throughout his life, he was always restless and hurried;
as soon as he managed to settle in a courtyard, he would break away from it. Now, he has come forth again from upon this hanging scroll—truly, who can know him?"
Death is life.
○ Master Yong of Mukan was a junior disciple of the Venerable Zhang of Fuzhou. Having abandoned Confucianism to follow the Buddha-dharma, he became friends with his dharma-brother Anfen.
Together they studied under Lan’an Xu at Yangyu, where both attained great enlightenment. Consequently, he composed [this verse]:
The Verse on the Water Conduit says: "The path winds around the head of ten-thousand-fathom cliffs; Carrying spring water and wearing the moon, when will it ever cease?
In this midst, if one can pivot and turn the aperture that pierces heaven, The person remains at ease while the water flows of itself.

When Miaoxi saw this, he said, "If Dingxu has such a son, the Dharma lineage of Yangqi will not fall into desolation. Later, when [Miaoxi] resided at Gushan, his brothers Jiang and Xi both entered [his assembly].
Ling, Songyuan, Wuyong, Xianan, and other elders were all among his disciples. Later, he passed away in Southern Quanzhou. Zhidao was a native of Anzhou.
Initially, he visited Miaoxi at the foot of Huiguan Peak. Miaoxi asked, "Who is this venerable monk?
Zhidao replied, "A man from Anzhou. Miaoxi said, "I have heard that the people of Anzhou are skilled at wrestling."
Fashi asked, "Is it so? Zhi immediately assumed a wrestling stance. Xuanji said, "People of Hunan eat fish; people of Hubei suffer from fish-bones. Zhi performed a backflip and left.
Xuanji remarked, "Who would have known that a single grain of bean would burst from cold ashes? Eventually, he took his leave of Xuanji and crossed the Yangtze River to Zhejiang.
He once traveled as a companion with Sanqu Shengshi and another person. Later, he resided at Baoning Temple in Jinling.

He succeeded to Miaoxi, and the Way of the Dharma flourished greatly. Consequently, while serving as a military governor, Chancellor Chen Junqing convened the abbots of various mountains for a tea ceremony.
Chen raised the phrase, "The 'having' and 'not having' [the word]—like a vine leaning against a tree," and commanded the abbots to offer critical commentaries.
All the abbots used sharp wit and clever speech to seek the Chancellor's favor; only the Master, at the very end, offered this verse: "Zhang beats the oil; Li beats the oil."
"He does not strike the whole body, but strikes only the head. The Prime Minister was greatly pleased. Before long, he moved to reside at Mount Jiangshan.
*Huigan Ti* (Or-an Ti) was a native of Huangyan, Taizhou. By nature he was coarse and rough, yet he dared to act decisively when faced with matters.
His monastic name was Ti Luanrao (Body-Disorderly-Disturbance). He studied under Ciyun Yuanwu Keqin at Huguo Temple. One day, while he was in the Hall of the Arhats...
While he was practicing the Way, he suddenly heard someone below the storehouse striking a fellow practitioner. He let out a great cry, and in that instant, he attained sudden enlightenment.
He ran to see Yuan, who said, "This Eleventh Brother has today, like a sick man, obtained a sweating cure. Not long after, he was appointed as the Director of Guests.

Later, Yuan ordered him to go out to solicit donations for the cultivation of fields, sending him off with this verse: "Vertically erecting three eyes upon the crown of his head, He unfurls the talisman from behind his elbow to test men."
"At the tip of the staff, there is not much more to life or death; to cut through the sea, one must be a true man of great character.
Thereafter, he relied upon Xiatang and served as the head of the assembly at Huqiu. He entered the world at Juebao in Suzhou, succeeding Cian, and his Dharma path flourished greatly.

Later, he moved to Jiaoshan, where the Prefectural Governor, Minister Zeng Zhonggong, frequently sought instruction from him. When the Master passed away, he entrusted a stone inkstone to [his successor].
Once, [Zhao] Meng composed a verse in his lament: "Fluttering, a single sandal pursues the west wind; Not a single thing remains within the cloth bag.
Leaving behind only the inkstone—what will you use? In old age, with no brush, how shall you judge the void?
When Tiyi was departing this world, he said: "An iron tree blooms; a rooster lays an egg. Seventy-two years, and the cradle rope has snapped. This may truly be called the spirit of Linji.
This is a metaphor for planting grass.
○ Initially, Heshang Xuedou Yuan resided at Jinsan Mountain in Wuzhou. Later, he accepted an invitation to serve as abbot at Chanji Temple in Jiankang.

While traveling through Sanqu, he passed by where Xuetang Xing was staying at Wugu. Yuan went there to discuss matters with his dharma relative; Xing conversed with him and marveled at his extraordinary character. Furthermore—
Having stayed for over ten days, he hurried to the prefectural seat to see the Layman Chaoran. He said, "The Master-Brother, Master Yuanwu, has a late disciple named Chuanyuan.
He arrived at the mountain yesterday and was about to depart to accept an invitation from Jiankang. I regret that his dwelling is in such a deep and remote location;
could you, Layman, petition the Prefect on my behalf to grant him a monastery so that he may remain? Chaoran immediately informed the Prefect.

The Prefect ordered that he reside at Dingye Chan Temple in Zihu. Having accepted the invitation, the Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Willingly accepting my lot as a golden-scaled fish, I remain trapped by the stump;
I have mistakenly caused others to abandon their meditative stillness for a distant summons. Now, midway through this journey, I again receive the command of the worthy Prefect;
it is difficult to avoid staying at Zihu at Dingye. Not long after, he was transferred to Baoen. At that time, Miaoxi was residing in Hengyang and had heard of the Master’s reputation. Because...
He sent his Dharma robes along with a verse, saying: "This fellow is a coarse rustic; neither true nor false. With this single white staff, he strikes even if it be the Buddha who comes.
Furthermore, he has another special quality: he knows how to gallop a horse within a begging bowl. Subsequently, he traveled to and resided at various mountains.
He received an imperial decree to reside at Lingyin.
○ Chan Master Mianjie was a native of Min. When he first crossed the mountain ridges, he arrived at Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou; while he was there, he happened to be basking in the sun.
An elder asked, "Where are you going on this journey, Venerable? He replied, "I am going to see Master Fozhi at Yuyang Monastery in Siming.
The elder said, "The world is in decline and the Way is lost. When young monks travel on pilgrimage nowadays, they generally bring their ears but not their eyes.
Jie asked, "What do you mean by that? The elder said, "Now there are a thousand people in the assembly at Yuyang. Every day, the Elder..."
We are so busy attending to one another that there is no leisure; how could we possibly find the opportunity to truly provide you with a catalyst for awakening?
Jie shed tears and said, "If this is the case, where should I go now? Xiu said, "From here, go to Mingguo in Quzhou.

The wind could not enter. Huairang was undaunted by the hardship. One day, in the room, he asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye?

Regarding the previous phrase, "The stone previously shattered and split," Jie stayed at Huajian for four years, exhausting the life-vein of a thousand sages.
When his mother grew old and he returned to his hometown, Huajian sent him off with this verse: "The phrase of great penetration that hits the mark, Directly facing, opens wide the crown of the head.

We followed you for four years; Your interrogations were thorough, leaving no trace. Though the dharma-bag has not yet been entrusted, Your spirit and bearing swallow heaven and earth. He then took up the correct...

I have a final word; when you return, I require that you follow it. Later, he emerged into the world at Wugu in Quzhou, where students gathered like clouds. He ascended the hall and said:
From the beginning, he never sang songs of empty delusions. He would carry fire to burn the mountains and gather field snails;

fish gave birth atop the white-boned trees, and birds built nests on the rapids of swift waters. All these were said to have been heard by him at night while he was clearly awake as a woodcutter singing;
thus he broke open the lacquer bucket. Indeed, the Master’s subtle mechanisms were unfathomable. Throughout his life, he resided in seven great monasteries, finally passing away at Taibai.

At the end of the summer retreat, he returned to his hometown because his mother was elderly and took his leave of Xuetang.
Master Tang sent him off with this verse: "Old Yan, in years past, exhausted himself investigating phenomena; He cast off his sandals to travel south and seek out the Patriarchal Masters.

Chan Master Ren, whose resolute will is peerless— He has come to visit me here in the state of Bai-lian on the green mountains. Amidst the surging of ten thousand waves and a thousand ripples, Truly, even a call does not reach him."
Turning back, he said, "The old man of West Mountain hopes we may dwell together. He also spoke of seeking the mountain paths of Yue once more;

He once composed a verse on the story of the Old Lady of Mount Tai, which scholars vied with one another to recite:
"He opened a shop for lamp-cotton and soap nuts, Seeking daily a few pints to pass the mornings and evenings. Only because of the long-continued torrential rains, The principal and the interest..."
A lone person leans against the gate in sorrowful contemplation. Lü Gongzheng of Xianmu had once sought instruction from the Master.
Upon parting, he asked for a verse. The Master took up his brush and presented this gift: "You have now arrived intimately at Changlu; Shaking out your robes, you possess not a single thing.

Later, he saw Sīxīn (Sishen), who raised the story of Yúnmén’s "falling into a pit. [Zhaozhou] penetrated the source of the Dharma profoundly; yet he did not forget Kāifú.

"Letting go at the precipice to distinguish the fish from the dragon; people only look at the fishing line, failing to see the reeds facing the red smartweed.
Guishan Dan first studied under Master Foxing Tai. One day, as the Master ascended the hall, he cited Zhaozhou’s saying: "The Terrace..."

"I vow to return without weariness. Subsequently, he appeared again at Nanzhao. Miaoxi praised him for this. Regarding Zen Master Lan’an Xu:
he followed the master Foxin Cai. When Cai resided at Dacheng, Xu had already been leading the assembly and had his name-board hung up there.
Later, when he was asked about the circumstances regarding the teaching "the mind is itself Buddha," Miaoxi was staying at Yan-yu Hermitage.
A friend of his named Guang Zhuangyuan wrote a letter to him, saying: "The master’s methods differ from those of other quarters;

you should come here for a brief visit. Miaoxi smiled but did not reply. Guang used this pretext to invite the Master to a meal. When Miaoxi went to attend, he reached the gate just as the assembly had gathered.
When Miaoxi opened his room for instruction, Xu followed the assembly. Miaoxi asked him, "A monk asked Mazu, 'What is the Buddha? Mazu replied, 'This very mind is the Buddha.
What do you say to this? Xu offered a response. Miaoxi rebuked him, saying, "With such a level of understanding, how dare you presume to act as a teacher to others?
He then had the drum beaten to assemble the entire community and exposed the depths of Xu's lifelong attainments, stripping away his false views.
Huineng was moved to tears that flowed down his cheeks; he did not dare look up at him and thought silently to himself: "That which I have attained has already been cast aside by this master.
Could the essential meaning of the West’s transmission truly be no more than this? He then resolved to place his heart in the ranks of Huineng’s disciples.
One day, Huineng asked with joy, "When there is neither letting out from within nor letting in from without—just at such a moment as this, what is it like? Huineng [remained silent].
Xuanze prepared to answer. Xixi took up his bamboo staff and struck him several times across the spine. Xu suddenly attained great enlightenment and said, "Master, you have already given me too much.
Xixi struck him once more. Xu prostrated himself. Xixi laughed and said, "Only today do I know that I have not deceived you.
He then bestowed upon him a seal in verse: "Body and mind are as one; Outside the body there is nothing else. Tsk! You blind donkey! He then transmitted [the Dharma] to him.

He received the *Dingxu* (Record of Dingxu), from which time his reputation resounded throughout the monastic community. He entered the world to reside at Yanfu in Quanzhou, and later moved to Xichan.
He once addressed the assembly, saying: "A sword hangs in the great void to manifest our school. Yet, while you sit with the majestic posture of meditation, how can you draw near?

Even if you possess the skillful means to turn earth into heaven and move like lightning or shooting stars, such techniques are nonetheless insufficient to withstand a formidable opponent. And now..."
"Is there anyone here who can distinguish between good and ill fortune? Come forth and meet me! If you hesitate for even a moment, I shall strike you once and smash you to pieces!
[He lets out a shout and descends from his seat. On another festival day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Before the twenty-fifth day, the multitude of yin energies recede and subside;
the mud-dragon closes its door. After the twenty-fifth day, the single yang returns; the iron tree blooms with flowers."

Precisely on the twenty-fifth day, those intoxicated guests amidst the dust—whether riding donkeys or horses through the streets and alleys before and behind—exchange congratulations with one another.
Yet the idle person beyond the mundane world, wrapped in a patched robe with his head covered, sits in meditation by the hearth; the wind whistles and the rain patters.
How cold and indifferent! Who cares about you, Master Zhang, Daoist Li, or Bodhidharma Hu? Again, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Holding Mohe Yan crosswise, you vainly display your haughty spirit; piercing through the azure void, you merely waste your energy.
Even if you do not move the blade of your spirit and bring about peace and prosperity by mere sitting, even the reigns of Emperors Yao and Shun still had their transformative influence remaining."
During the Shaoxing era, there was an official who visited Jiaoshan and inscribed a poem on the Fengyue Pavilion (Wind and Moon Pavilion), which read:

"Wind comes from the treetops, pure and hard to stand; Moon arrives at the heart of the waves, faint and about to sink. If one realizes that the pine wind is originally beyond the mundane world, Only then will one know that the river moon resembles my own mind.
All who viewed it before and after praised it without exception, except for Guyuan Guo, who arrived there while traveling on pilgrimage.
Guan said, "The poem is well-written, yet it simply lacks the 'eye'. A fellow practitioner asked, "Where is it that it lacks the eye?
Guo replied, "If I were to change two characters for him, you would immediately see the eye. The fellow practitioner asked, "Which characters should be changed?
Guo said, "Why not say: 'Only when one realizes that the wind in the pines is not outside of things, does one know that the moon over the river is none other than oneself'?"
The mind! Those who were seated were deeply moved and believed it. For one whose "work" has opened their eyes, the perspective is naturally different.
Moreover, Master Yue’an had never practiced poetry in his life, yet he could inspire such transformation;

is this not like a dragon king who, having obtained but a single drop of water, can raise clouds and mist? Brothers, as you travel on foot, you must discern the fundamental reality beneath your robes.

As for the division of matters, it does not lie in attacking external studies. After a long time, the eye opens, and one naturally pierces through to the very eyes of all Buddhas—how much more so regarding worldly texts?
When Chan Master Hongzhi resided at Yuan Tong, he dreamed one night of composing a couplet: "The pine path is secluded and deep;
when one arrives, the faint moon is in the midst of twilight. For several years thereafter, he had no further inkling of this dream. During the Jianyan era...

Fleeing from the rebels, he crossed East Zhejiang under a single straw hat and arrived at Tiantong. Just as the incumbent abbot had vacated his seat, the Master entered the mountain from his boat at the break of dawn;

it was precisely the hour when daybreak dawns. Seeing the pine-lined path desolate and dense, and the moonlight veiled in mist and haze, he suddenly realized the lines of the dream he had previously experienced.
Upon returning to the guest quarters (*danguo*), although he did not mention his name, his fellow monks already [knew him].
An observer remarked, "This is the Elder of Changlu; why has he come here? He secretly informed the administrator, who immediately reported it to the Prefectural Office.
The Prefect was overjoyed, for he had dreamed the night before that a divine being had informed him: "The master of Tiantong is an ancient Buddha of Xizhou.
He immediately issued a formal notice and dispatched an official to the guest quarters to invite the Master. The Master firmly refused.

Consequently, his fellow monks at the guest quarters carried him back to the abbot’s quarters by force. He remained there for thirty years, and from this point on, the lineage of Dongshan flourished greatly.
Thus, one should know that the conditions for a person’s tenure in a monastery are determined by their own karmic destiny; they do not depend on seeking office through improper means.
Master Yuanji Cen was a native of Xianju in Taizhou. He possessed a solitary loftiness of character and integrity that few have matched in recent times.

For many years he relied upon Master Ruyun at Yunju, serving in the library office for seventeen years. After Ruyun passed away, he traveled with his single staff back to Zhejiang and relied upon Master Zhengtang Bian at Daochang Monastery.
Not long after, he was appointed by Master Dongzu Yuan to take charge of the world-renowned Bianshan in Xie. This was [the monastery of] Shishi...
This single incense offering is presented to commemorate the place where Master Lin lectured on the *Yi Jing*, thereby clarifying his intent.

Although Cen eventually succeeded Yunju Ru, he was highly esteemed by the monastic community. Later, he presided over several great monasteries; however, his karmic fortune was obstructed, and he encountered many hardships throughout his life.
Yet, Cen never let these matters trouble him. Throughout his life, he never even glanced at offerings or profits. Later, he retired to Chang...

He passed away at the Huazang (Flower Treasury) Dharma Hall. His *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) in twenty fascicles circulates in the world, with the Prefectural Secretary, Master Zeng Zhonggong, having composed a preface for its opening.
Qian Chen has also written a eulogy for Changlu Jianzang; that eulogy says: "At midnight he pushed forth the sun’s orb;
At dawn he grasped the moon’s chariot. Taking up the four continents, He placed them within a single grain of millet. [End of excerpt]
It is like playing music without strings, yet not the "Treading on Frost" melody; singing a Hu song, yet not the "White Snow" aria.

Master Honyuan Mi resided at Zituo. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mountain clouds are vast and dim; the lofty trees cast dense shadows. The ancient buildings stand solemnly;
the monastic groves are silent and still. Here, Honyuan plants thorns and scatters prickly-egrets, blocking the way with stubborn obstructions.
Who dares to look upon this with the true eye? Suddenly, if there is a man who can turn his body and breathe forth here," [he would be one].
Three or five bowls of strong tea—my intent lies at the edge of the mattock. If this is not yet so, then on the steep path of the green peaks one gazes upon the azure void;
do not say that I, the Elder, have not told you. He also said: "The spring days are warm, the yellow orioles sing; listen further to the sound of the water falling from the precipice.

How can one bring up a single phrase? Bending the arm to use the fist as a pillow, lying down to hear the evening bell.
Fu Zhenggong Bi studied under Chan Master Touzi Yong, observing the etiquette of a disciple with the utmost reverence and integrity, just like a novice.
Later, because Zhang Bishu Yin used his power and status to treat the monastics with contempt, Zhenggong wrote to him, saying:
Among those of the Chan school, whenever they encounter discourse that is overly prolix and lacks directness, they call it "entanglements" (geteng) and often treat it with disdain and ridicule;
consequently, [Zhao]zhou composed the "Song of Entanglements" (contained in his collected works). I, Bi, have long reflected upon the reasons for this and now venture to discuss it with Youyin.
I do not know what you think. Generally speaking, there is not the slightest difference between the nature and understanding of worldly scholars and monastics.

There are differences; their life stories contain many points of significant divergence. For instance, monks leave home at a young age and, having spent long years studying the scriptures from an early time, their knowledge and experience consist entirely of Buddhist matters.
After shaving their heads, they travel in groups on pilgrimage, going wherever they wish to reach.
Beyond practicing meditation and seeking the Way, the breadth and depth of what the multitude has seen and heard is moreover limitless to the ears and eyes.
Once the fumes have fully ripened, if one suddenly encounters a person of clear vision who plucks it out, one immediately gains a point of insight.
One can then take all that has been previously seen and heard as personal evidence; is this not brilliantly clear and exhilarating?
We worldly folk, from our youth, have been steeped in mundane affairs; upon reaching adulthood, we further marry and raise children, busying ourselves with worldly pursuits.
Preoccupied with clothing and food, they run about in pursuit of official posts; the yellow scrolls and red volumes have never entered their hands.
Even when they do find leisure to peruse them, it is merely for the sake of providing material for conversation; how could they ever penetrate to the depths of their principles?

Furthermore, as members of the four classes—scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants—each bound by their respective vocations, even if they were to know of the Dharma assemblies in Zen groves and wished to go there to seek instruction, by what means could they possibly go? How?
Furthermore, are there many who have traveled together to the mountains to practice Chan and inquire about the Way, or who have engaged extensively in communal study and discipline?
Even if one were to encounter a person of clear vision through some circumstance, if they lack even a single flavor of genuine practice, how much could they possibly have heard?

What has one actually attained? Furthermore, regarding what is seen and heard, there is no questioning; one takes one's own experience as evidence and does not further engage in extensive inquiry or study.

Having merely pored over and revered the teachings until gaining a single word or half-phrase—yet still far from clear understanding—one immediately gazes at the clouds in the sky and looks up toward heaven through the nostrils, claiming, "I transcend the Buddhas and surpass the Patriarchs; all the sages must stand beneath me."

Feng, you utterly disregard the Buddhist scriptures and Chan records, doing so merely to avoid being accused of "entanglement" (*ge-teng*). From my humble perspective, I deeply fear that this is not the case.

If I, Bi, were to study at all, and were to study it through the discernment of body and mind, it would require a thorough and meticulous engagement—probing deeply and searching far, penetrating to the very summit and the very bottom, reaching the very bone and the very marrow, until everything is spontaneously realized as luminous clarity.
Purity. Only when you have utterly severed even a speck of dust or a trace of obscuration may you dare to conceal it—conceal it! This one matter is no small thing;
it requires that you directly cast off the root of birth and death since beginningless time and stand as an adversary to the Old Man Yama, who governs birth and death.
You must not take idle talk or long-winded words from others to substitute for this.
Studying the Way, one simply deceives oneself. *Zhuzhu*. Bi respectfully submits this to the officials of the Bureau of Rites.

Jing said, "That is just furniture for leisure. Qing asked, "Do you not want what is urgent? Jing said, "Try bringing it out and see.
Qing gave a single strike with his sitting mat and departed. Jing was greatly startled by this. Later, he appeared in the world at Huanglong. (From *Shang*)
The Master said: "Yesterday I was a guest in the forest; this morning I am the abbot upon the dais. To let go or to gather in is entirely up to me;
